titulo: Quiz — Bar, table and the bill
subtitulo: One evening in a Madrid bar, from the door to the last euro
introPt: Quiz time. Two of you walk into a busy bar in Madrid at nine in the evening. You greet the room, check the price at the counter, order, get the real menu, avoid ordering dinner for six, drink water you don't pay for, refuse bread you didn't ask for, and query one line on the bill. Listen as many times as you like, then answer.
cenario: A couple walks into a Spanish bar in the evening: they greet, check whether the terrace costs more, order drinks, ask for the menu, sort out portion sizes, get tap water, decline the bread, ask for the bill and query a charge.

dialogo.pt: — Evening. (you, walking in — greeting the room is not optional)
— Hi! Go ahead. (the barman: 'dime' means it's your turn)

dialogo.es: ¿Es el mismo precio en la barra?
dialogo.pinyin: es el MEES-moh PREH-thyoh en lah BAH-rrah
dialogo.pt: — Is it the same price at the counter?

dialogo.es: En la terraza hay suplemento. En la barra no.
dialogo.pinyin: en lah teh-RRAH-thah ai soo-pleh-MEN-toh — en lah BAH-rrah noh
dialogo.pt: — There's a surcharge on the terrace. Not at the counter.

dialogo.es: Vale. ¿Me pones dos cañas, por favor?
dialogo.pinyin: BAH-leh — meh POH-nehs dohs KAH-nyahs, por fah-BOR
dialogo.pt: — Fine. Could I have two small beers, please?
— And could we have the menu? (la carta — not 'el menú')

dialogo.es: Aquí tienes. Hoy hay pulpo, muy bueno.
dialogo.pinyin: ah-KEE TYEH-nehs — oy ai POOL-poh, mwee BWEH-noh
dialogo.pt: — Here you are. We've got octopus today, very good.

dialogo.es: ¿Esto es tapa, media ración o ración?
dialogo.pinyin: EHS-toh es TAH-pah, MEH-dhyah rrah-THYON oh rrah-THYON
dialogo.pt: — Is that a tapa, a half portion or a full one?
— Full portion. It's big, for sharing.

dialogo.es: Entonces media ración. Y una jarra de agua del grifo, por favor.
dialogo.pinyin: en-TOHN-thehs MEH-dhyah rrah-THYON — ee OO-nah KHAH-rrah deh AH-gwah del GREE-foh
dialogo.pt: — Half a portion then. And a jug of tap water, please.

dialogo.es: El pan no, gracias. No queremos pan.
dialogo.pinyin: el pahn noh, GRAH-thyahs — noh keh-REH-mohs pahn
dialogo.pt: — No bread, thanks. We don't want bread.
— Can we settle up, please? (the bill is never coming on its own)

dialogo.es: Perdone, creo que hay un error. Esto no lo hemos pedido.
dialogo.pinyin: pehr-DOH-neh, KREH-oh keh ai oon eh-RROR — EHS-toh noh loh EH-mohs peh-DEE-dhoh
dialogo.pt: — Sorry, I think there's a mistake. We didn't order this.

perguntas.pergunta: The barman says «Dime». What is he doing?
perguntas.es: The barman says «Dime». What is he doing?
opcoes: Telling you the bar is full
Telling you it's your turn — order now
Asking for your name
Asking whether you want the terrace
perguntas.explica: «Dime» literally means 'tell me', and it is the exact moment you're supposed to speak. Look up, make eye contact, order. Wait politely for something longer and someone else gets served.
perguntas.pt: «Dime» literally means 'tell me', and it is the exact moment you're supposed to speak. Look up, make eye contact, order. Wait politely for something longer and someone else gets served.

perguntas.pergunta: Why does she ask «¿Es el mismo precio en la barra?» before sitting down?
perguntas.es: Why does she ask «¿Es el mismo precio en la barra?» before sitting down?
opcoes: Because charging different prices for the counter, the table and the terrace is illegal
Because it's a way of asking for a discount
Because the same drink can legally cost three different prices, and the surcharge only has to be on the posted list
Because the terrace is always cheaper
perguntas.explica: Barra, mesa and terraza can legally carry different prices — as long as it's shown on the price list. Ask before you sit, not after you've paid: once it's posted, you have no complaint.
perguntas.pt: Barra, mesa and terraza can legally carry different prices — as long as it's shown on the price list. Ask before you sit, not after you've paid: once it's posted, you have no complaint.

perguntas.pergunta: She asks for «la carta». What would she have got if she'd asked for «el menú»?
perguntas.es: She asks for «la carta». What would she have got if she'd asked for «el menú»?
opcoes: Exactly the same thing — they're synonyms
The set meal at a fixed price, ordered on her behalf
The wine list
The bill
perguntas.explica: The daily false friend. «La carta» is the list of everything the kitchen can make; «el menú» is a specific set meal at a fixed price — and asking for it counts as ordering it. Nobody will correct you.
perguntas.pt: The daily false friend. «La carta» is the list of everything the kitchen can make; «el menú» is a specific set meal at a fixed price — and asking for it counts as ordering it. Nobody will correct you.

perguntas.pergunta: The barman says the octopus is a «ración». Why does she switch to «media ración»?
perguntas.es: The barman says the octopus is a «ración». Why does she switch to «media ración»?
opcoes: Because a ración is a small nibble and she wants more
Because a ración is a large sharing plate and there are only two of them
Because raciones are only served at lunchtime
Because a ración always contains ham
perguntas.explica: Tapa small, pincho on bread and counted by the stick, media ración right for two, ración enough for four. Reading 'ración' as 'nibble' is how two people end up ordering dinner for six.
perguntas.pt: Tapa small, pincho on bread and counted by the stick, media ración right for two, ración enough for four. Reading 'ración' as 'nibble' is how two people end up ordering dinner for six.

perguntas.pergunta: She orders «una jarra de agua del grifo». What's true about that in Spain?
perguntas.es: She orders «una jarra de agua del grifo». What's true about that in Spain?
opcoes: It's a cheeky request that some places allow
Bars must offer free unpackaged water on request — it's the law since 2022
It's only free if you've ordered food
It's free but only at the counter, never at a table
perguntas.explica: Since 2022 hospitality venues have had to offer free unpackaged water. Ask for a «jarra» — a jug — rather than a glass. If they flatly refuse, that's a complaint-form situation.
perguntas.pt: Since 2022 hospitality venues have had to offer free unpackaged water. Ask for a «jarra» — a jug — rather than a glass. If they flatly refuse, that's a complaint-form situation.

perguntas.pergunta: The total is «veinticinco con cincuenta». How much is that?
perguntas.es: The total is «veinticinco con cincuenta». How much is that?
perguntas.explica: Twenty-five fifty. Both halves carry the Spanish 'th' of «think» — cin-co, cin-cuenta. Miss it and «cincuenta» (50) turns into «sesenta» (60). Four of the numbers on every bar bill have that sound in them.
perguntas.pt: Twenty-five fifty. Both halves carry the Spanish 'th' of «think» — cin-co, cin-cuenta. Miss it and «cincuenta» (50) turns into «sesenta» (60). Four of the numbers on every bar bill have that sound in them.

perguntas.pergunta: «Perdone, creo que hay un error… esto no lo hemos pedido.» If the waiter still refuses, what's the next step?
perguntas.es: «Perdone, creo que hay un error… esto no lo hemos pedido.» If the waiter still refuses, what's the next step?
opcoes: Raise your voice so other customers hear
Refuse to pay and walk out
Ask, calmly and still sitting down, for «la hoja de reclamaciones»
Leave a bad review and forget it
perguntas.explica: Six words, said in the same tone as 'could we have the menu': «La hoja de reclamaciones, por favor.» It's an official form in triplicate, one copy of which goes to the regional consumer authority that licenses the place — and refusing to hand it over is itself a serious offence. Sitting down, normal volume. A shouting tourist is entertainment; a calm one asking for a government form is a problem.
perguntas.pt: Six words, said in the same tone as 'could we have the menu': «La hoja de reclamaciones, por favor.» It's an official form in triplicate, one copy of which goes to the regional consumer authority that licenses the place — and refusing to hand it over is itself a serious offence. Sitting down, normal volume. A shouting tourist is entertainment; a calm one asking for a government form is a problem.
